Q: How to fix 22: error: not found: value SparkSession in Scala? A:

SparkSession is available in spark 2. No need to create sparkcontext in spark version 2. sparksession itself provides the gateway to all .

Q: Find list of values in list of values A:

While it is not exactly clear what you want to do with the data, since you are using SQL Server my suggestion would be to use the UNPIVOT function to turn the col1, col2 and col3 columns into rows which will make it easier to filter the data:

select db, name, type, col, value
from foo
unpivot
(
  value
  for col in (Col1, Col2, Col3)
) unpiv;

See SQL Fiddle with Demo. This gives the data in the following format:

| DB | NAME |  TYPE |  COL | VALUE |
------------------------------------
|  4 |  AC1 |    LO | Col1 |     1 |
|  4 |  AC1 |    LO | Col2 |    10 |
|  4 |  AC1 |    LO | Col3 |     2 |
|  4 |  AC1 |    HI | Col1 |     2 |

Once the is in the row format, it should be significantly easier to apply any filters or even join to your BAR table.

Q: i want to integrate ai into my food delivery logistics platform, how do i start A:

Just to clarify, you only want a chat bot that helps customers, not an AI agent. So while I understand you need/seek code and possibly CI/CD setup, until you reach that point, IMO you'll need a small design and analysis document where you need to specify your expectations (i.e. what you assume or want or whatever, the LLM to do). After that, you'll need to ALWAYS grant exactly the access it needs, nothing more.

For example, consider only logged in users can use the chatbot (or if you want it available to others that are not authenticated - which I don't recommend, have restricted access, but the issue with this is there might be a 0.0000001% chance of either hallucination or accessing a separate user's account data, depending on how you setup the comms between the LLM and your components, such as DB, webapp, etc.).

So from there, you'd prolly need to see what order is in progress or if you want some sort of complaint system, then the LLM would need to see past/finalized orders too.

Here is where it gets tricky: if you want it to only give advice (i.e. "you have some sort of issue, in order to fix it do this, that, x, y"), then this is enough. If you want stuff like if the payment fails and the customer wants to retry, cancel the order, add something else, whatever other crazy stuff from an LLM prompt, then you can't do it. You'll need an AI Agent. And this is where it gets tricky as you'll need to make sure it has only read-only rights, unless you want to have some nasty surprises.

Back to customer help-only, The LLM will need to be trained on your mechanics/flows. For instance how to cancel an order manually, how to do X, Y, Z.

Then you have the model which can either be a SaaS (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, etc.), or your own (that you deploy on-prem if you have a good server setup or on a PaaS). When I mean "your own" I don't literally mean "one made by you", but there are models that have minimal training and are targeted at businesses that would train it for whatever they need to do. The difference is, and I kid you not, if you'll use Claude or ChatGPT a user can literally ask it "how do I make an omelette" or even "how do I fix this C++/java/C#/python error?" and it would give the recipe and instructions or steps to fix the coding error. While it might seem funny to you, remember this does cost you usage. And the usage is not the one you had in mind.

Then you'd need to take into account languages. Because you don't know what customers you have (consider tourists or if you expand abroad).

My point is, before you ask "I want code and advice on how to integrate", I think you need to plan this first. It's not quite "drag and drop" or "plug 'n' play" (depending on your age, you might get the references). Normally you'd need an architect, a technical analyst, a dev, obviously some legal guys that know privacy policies and AI Act (this also depends on your location as GDPR might be a factor or the AI act might not be) and obviously liability (remember that the chat bot must explicitly say they are an LLM, they might be beta and they might make mistakes unless you want serious legal issues - technically speaking, if you opt for a SaaS like ChatGPT, there are also some "less fortunate situations" surrounding it, security guys, network guys, obviously some people that know cloud infrastructure and the list goes on.

So if I am to just answer you on how do I start?, the answer is: "planning first, analysis next, etc.". Oh, I didn't even mention you'll need a separate budget for this. So there's also that.

And keep in mind we didn't even reach the code part yet.
